docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Compatibility / Qualification status / September 19, 2026

docs.title: No qualified model yet.
docs.text:
Current Status: Zero real Intel Macs have completed NextCore product qualification. There is no supported model list for the engineering preview. macOS boot, physical desktop, Metal and installation acceptance remain false.

Target State: A documented set of real Intel Macs with model-specific admission, installation, reboot, graphics and recovery evidence for each claimed capability.

Default release-policy preview

docs.title: Unsupported or unqualified platforms are refused.
docs.text: The public ISO and EFI use the default release policy. No hardware family has been qualified for installation. A refusal is not a completed installation or a successful compatibility test.

docs.title: Intended hardware scope
docs.text:
The project targets macOS 27 through the unfinished NextCore compatibility layer on real Intel Macs. This is a development objective, not a claim that Apple's native support policy includes those machines or that NextCore currently runs the OS on them.

Generic PCs and virtual machines are not release installation targets. Internal OVMF tests provide repeatable firmware checks; they do not qualify a physical Mac. An Apple-silicon computer is not a substitute for the required real Intel Mac acceptance target.

The archived firmware ZIP predates the current policy. Its existence does not establish support for any platform or mean that it enforces the current release restrictions.

docs.title: Hardware admission
docs.text: Identify the real machine and supported configuration, validate the admission decision, and test refusal paths. Model names, serial strings and copied SMBIOS identifiers alone do not prove genuine Apple hardware. One VM refusal does not establish universal non-Mac exclusion.

docs.title: Installation and reboot
docs.text: Bind explicit confirmation to the exact target device and proposed changes. Verify writes, preserve unrelated disks, handle interruptions, and demonstrate a working installed-system reboot on the identified computer.

docs.title: Usable operating system and graphics
docs.text: Verify target-matching macOS kernel and userspace, visible interaction, and the device functions being claimed. Metal needs actual guest device creation, submitted work, completion and correct output. Firmware display or a client build is insufficient.

docs.title: Recovery appropriate to the hardware
docs.text: Qualify Recovery and any applicable DFU operation separately. Native DFU depends on the hardware; ordinary Intel EFI Recovery is not Apple-silicon DFU. Neither capability is currently accepted.

docs.title: Reading a future support entry
docs.text:
A support entry will need an identified model and configuration, the tested release, the demonstrated operations and their limits. A model catalog, an EFI launch or a screenshot alone cannot supply that evidence. Until qualification is complete, the status stays unverified.

docs.title: Installation Utility engineering preview
docs.text:
Release target: engineering-preview-20260919 in 26x86/NextCore. Channel: preview. The ISO and EFI both use the default release-policy build. This profile refuses unsupported or unqualified platforms; it is distinct from the internal research profile used for OVMF planning and read-only GPT tests.

Open the preview release and published assets

Use the release asset list to confirm publication and file availability. The website's link is not a completed download or validation receipt.

The exact 17,641,472-byte ISO was executed under QEMU/OVMF: the utility started and refused the unsupported virtual machine. Its SHA-256 is cd79ef7bfbc8fc3273064662472a37073b0dfa47ace119527b27e08413a4c62f. This bounded refusal check does not qualify any physical Mac or demonstrate installation. The download catalog records final sizes and hashes for each published asset.

docs.title: Check a download
docs.text:
1. Confirm the repository and exact release tag above.
  2. Download the selected asset, MANIFEST.sha256, release.json and LICENSES.txt from that same release.
  3. Compute the asset's SHA-256 and compare it with the matching filename in the manifest.
  4. Read the metadata and current acceptance limits. A matching checksum does not qualify a machine or authorize installation.

For example, use Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 .\nextcore-installation-preview.iso in PowerShell, or shasum -a 256 nextcore-installation-preview.iso on macOS. Compare the full value, ignoring letter case only.

docs.title: Archived engineering firmware
docs.text:
prebuiltefi.zip is a separate legacy artifact, not the current supported release. Its primary public EFI source revision is df2c15b8. The manifest pins all seven public module sources and separately identifies private assembly revision 3d3a434dfc9f84dcc1c34a2257f8cf7ceaafd99c; the complete assembly is not publicly downloadable. It predates the current real-Mac admission policy; do not assume it enforces the preview's hardware restrictions. It is not an installation recommendation or a compatibility approval.

Legacy prebuiltefi.zip Legacy archive hash and provenance

The archive contains a baseline EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI, an empty EFI/OC/config.plist, a separate diagnostics/NXARMJIT.efi, manifest.json, README.txt and embedded LICENSES.txt. Baseline firmware and the diagnostic are different artifacts; the diagnostic must not be relabeled as the normal boot entry. Neither establishes a working macOS installation.

The deployment builds and verifies this legacy archive from its pinned source selection. Its sidecar describes the actual deployed ZIP. Updating the portal or publishing the new utility preview does not update this pin or add the newer hardware policy to the old binaries.

docs.title: Release and publication policy
docs.text:
Preview is an engineering channel. Packaging an ISO or EFI does not promote macOS boot, Metal, installation or hardware acceptance. The current preview uses the default release policy; research profiles remain distinct. The archived firmware ZIP retains its own source pin and older policy.

Public guidance covers verified behavior, artifact identity and explicit limitations. Internal design and build plans, research notebooks, raw execution traces and local evidence are excluded from this site and its search index. Private source documents remain separate from the public guide.

docs.text: Public progress / Reviewed September 19, 2026

docs.title: What works. What remains.
docs.text:
Current Status: Partial firmware, client-build and utility-test results. Every product acceptance flag below remains false. Test counts describe specific checks; they are not a percentage of product completion.

Target State: Working macOS 27, functional Metal graphics and a complete Installation Utility on qualified real Intel Macs. Each deliverable requires its own execution evidence.

Current execution boundary

docs.title: Early firmware only. Product acceptance remains unverified.
docs.text: The latest real-media boot stops during firmware initialization. Metal clients cross-build; utility planning and read-only inspection run in an internal OVMF research profile. No verified macOS 27 installation, working Metal driver or qualified real Intel Mac is available.

docs.title: Reach early firmware
docs.text:
Real macOS 27 media reaches an early firmware stage, then stops during initialization. The current real-media result is firmware-stage execution only.

Observed: Early firmware execution has been observed. This does not establish macOS kernel or userspace startup.

Next: Resolve the initialization failure and demonstrate a repeatable transition to the target macOS kernel.

Acceptance: macOS boot remains unverified.

docs.title: Start macOS and reach a desktop
docs.text:
No verified macOS 27 kernel-to-userspace boot, installed-system reboot or interactive desktop on a real Intel Mac is available.

Observed: Earlier experiments and authored tests cover individual components. They do not satisfy the current macOS 27 acceptance target.

Next: Verify the target OS version, kernel and userspace in one boot, followed by installation, reboot and visible interaction on identified real hardware.

Acceptance: Boot and physical desktop acceptance are false.

docs.title: Run Metal work in the guest
docs.text:
Metal test clients cross-build successfully. Those clients are prerequisites for testing; they are not a working graphics driver.

Observed: Client builds and contract checks exist. A guest-visible Metal provider connected to a functioning driver has not been demonstrated.

Next: Create an actual guest Metal device and command queue, submit work, observe completion and verify rendered or computed results.

Acceptance: Metal acceptance is false. No performance target is required.

docs.title: Inspect a disk and review a plan
docs.text:
The internal utility exercises explicit target selection, planning and read-only GPT inspection under OVMF with 512-byte and 4096-byte sectors.

Observed: Read-only firmware checks and 36 EFI core tests cover this increment. Planning review, cancellation and inspection do not install anything.

Next: Connect the reviewed plan to independently verified firmware operations while preserving exact target identity and unrelated disks.

Acceptance: The public default release-policy preview is non-installing. Internal research results do not qualify its use on hardware.

docs.title: Apply and verify an installation
docs.text:
37 host tests pass for disposable disk-image creation and transaction handling. They exercise host tools, not physical disk installation from EFI.

Observed: Disposable-image tests cover bounded writes, verification and transaction recovery checks. EFI runtime apply and installed-system recovery remain unfinished.

Next: Implement exact-target confirmation, firmware writes, readback, interruption handling and applicable boot-entry setup; qualify Recovery and DFU separately where the hardware supports them.

Acceptance: Installation, Recovery and DFU acceptance are false.

docs.title: Qualify real Intel Mac hardware
docs.text:
No real Intel Mac has completed product qualification. There is no supported model list for this preview.

Observed: The exact downloadable preview ISO entered the default release-policy utility under QEMU/OVMF and refused the virtual machine without disk or NVRAM writes. A VM refusal test does not establish reliable real-Mac authentication.

Next: Validate admission and each claimed operation on identified real Intel Macs, including negative controls, installation, reboot and usable output.

Acceptance: Real-hardware qualification is false. Model strings alone are not proof of Apple hardware.

docs.title: Acceptance status
docs.text:
• macOS boot: false. Target-matching kernel and userspace execution are not verified for the current macOS 27 path.
  • Physical desktop: false. No verified installed-system reboot and interactive desktop on a real Intel Mac.
  • Metal: false. No demonstrated working guest driver with device creation, submitted work and correct observable results.
  • Installation: false. The utility does not perform a qualified physical installation.
  • Recovery: false. Hardware-specific preparation and recovery are not qualified.
  • DFU: false. Native DFU is hardware-dependent; ordinary Intel EFI Recovery is not Apple-silicon DFU.
  • Real-hardware qualification: false. No Intel Mac model has completed qualification.

docs.title: September 19 update
docs.text:
The utility now has a reviewed target-planning flow and read-only GPT inspection tested in OVMF with both 512-byte and 4096-byte sectors. Its 36 EFI core tests are separate from the 37 host tests for disposable-image writing and transaction handling. These results establish bounded engineering behavior, not EFI disk installation or a supported computer.

Metal test clients cross-build successfully. The outstanding work is the actual guest driver connection and observable execution. The latest real-media boot remains at an early firmware initialization failure; no new macOS boot success is claimed.

The engineering preview packages the default release-policy utility as an ISO and EFI ZIP with notices. The internal OVMF research profile is distinct. Release builds refuse unsupported or unqualified platforms, and no real Intel Mac has yet been qualified.

docs.title: How to read these results
docs.text:
Observed describes a completed check or execution. Next describes unfinished work. Acceptance states whether the product behavior has been demonstrated. Public summaries deliberately omit raw research traces and internal implementation details; they remain readable without private links.
